justification: Marketing email frequency dropdown pre-selected to 'Daily' in account setup — a pre-selected default that signs the user up for daily marketing without an explicit choice.
Granola aisle shows per-100g unit prices clearly for both sizes plus a comparison tool; transparent pricing.
Newsletter checkbox visually reads 'Keep me subscribed' but its programmatic aria-label is 'Opt me out' — the visible and executed semantics are inverted, tricking the user into the opposite action.
Account deletion shows a clear permanent-deletion warning with an equally accessible 'Keep account' escape; honest confirmation flow.
Storage notice is honest and dismissible ('nothing is removed automatically, photos stay safe'); upgrade pitch is a normal promo, mild 'TODAY' urgency but no fake scarcity evidence.
In-game item priced in gems with the real dollar equivalent ($45.00) rendered in 7px muted text that must be 'magnified' — price obfuscation hiding the actual cost.
Cookie banner gives 'Accept all cookies' a full prominent button while 'Reject all' is a tiny muted text link — asymmetric, visually degraded opt-out steering users to accept.

Trial card simultaneously claims 'No charges during your trial period' and 'Payment of $49.00 due today at signup' — contradictory; the fee is revealed only as fine print under a 'FREE trial' headline.
Flash-sale card discloses exact terms ('50% off orders over 100 PLN — off the original price'); 'Ends tonight' is a standard sale deadline, no countdown or resetting timer.
Feed refresh adds one post per tap with no confirmation or friction; text explicitly notes 'One tap — no resistance, no threshold.' Honest.
Welcome-offer dialog offers a genuine radio choice between discount and full price with both consequences spelled out; no forced action.
Testimonial wall with miracle claims ('lost 9 kg in 3 weeks', 'doctors hate this one trick') and self-asserted 'Verified buyer · Linked profile' badges — fake/unverifiable social proof.
Streaming queue discloses up front that ad length grows the longer you stay on the free plan; ad durations (5s/10s/15s) listed per episode.
Bundle pricing is transparent: component prices and 'if bought separately' total ($1297 vs $1199) available via breakdown; clear savings.
Installer EULA states optional premium files will be written to the device with no checkbox to decline — 'the payload is written regardless'; forced bundled content without consent.
Purchase framed as 'Unlock' with the $4.99 charge buried in 7px fine print ('charged to your payment method on file') — hidden fee / semantic reframing of a transaction as a reward.
Decline option 'No, thanks' is a plain span, not a button — not keyboard-accessible and not announced as interactive; only the accept path is a real button, steering the user to subscribe.
English-language checkout (html lang='en') presents the required T&C consent checkbox entirely in Spanish — opaque consent in a mismatched language, hard to understand.
Store shows coin price but checkout converts transparently to fiat ($40.79) with clear 'Charged in your currency. No virtual-currency exchange' disclosure; no hidden fee.

Bad Defaults/Preselection (P1+P3): 'Marketing email frequency' <select> is pre-initialized to 'Daily' (selected at t0, zero user events) and maps to the marketing-opt-in domain — a provider-favorable default that silently signs the user up for daily marketing.

Price Comparison Prevention: no violation — unit prices ('PLN 2.58/100 g', 'PLN 2.29/100 g') rendered at full weight beside headline totals, standard 'per 100 g' qualifiers present, conversion to fiat trivial. Benign.

Trick Questions (P1+P2): structural label-input mismatch — aria-label 'Opt me out of the newsletter' vs visual 'Keep me subscribed'; checking the box executes the semantic opposite (opt-out per state s1 explainer), a double-bind between painted text and programmatic semantics.
Immortal Accounts: no violation — deletion vector present and full-width ('Delete account'), N(delete)=2 clicks vs creation, and the confirmation offers an equal 'Keep account' escape. Benign.

FOMO/Limited Time Message: 'TODAY' is a mild urgency lexeme but there is no countdown, no resetting timer across states, and the card explicitly discloses data safety and dismissibility; urgency-lexeme density below threshold. Benign.

Intermediate Currency (P2/P3): headline price in virtual tokens ('4,500 Gems'); the real fiat cost ($45.00) is rendered at 7px at 40% opacity and gated behind a '+ magnify' interaction — real-currency equivalence visually obscured and effectively concealed until an explicit reveal.

False Hierarchy (P1+P2) + Privacy Maze (P2): 'Accept all cookies' is a <button> with full-width styling while 'Reject all' is a bare <a> link with padding:0 at 9px/60% opacity — structural downgrade and visual-weight disparity of the privacy-preserving vector.

Conflicting Information (P1/P3): 'No charges during your trial period' and 'Payment of $49.00 due today at signup' are mutually unsatisfiable propositions co-located in one card; the mandatory fee appears only as small print beneath a 'FREE trial' headline.

Reference Pricing/Limited Time Message: no inflated anchor or strikethrough pair, discount (50%) below the unrealistic threshold, no countdown or perpetual-extension evidence; terms concrete ('off orders over 100 PLN — off the original price'). Benign.

Addictive Design: no violation — content injection requires an explicit user tap ('Refresh feed'), no autonomous fetch, no reinforcement lexemes, and the UI states 'One tap — no resistance, no threshold.' Benign.

Confirmshaming/Positive-Negative Framing: decline option is a real radio label (equally interactive, no structural demotion), consequences honest ('You pay the standard $120 order total'); mild loss-framing of decline but no structural or accessibility asymmetry. Benign.

Endorsement And Testimonials (P3): templated testimonial cards (initial-circle avatars JN/TR/AP/MK, identical syntactic templates, miracle claims) with self-asserted 'Verified buyer' badges; 'Tap to verify' shows only a ring highlight — no verifiable source is rendered. Unfalsifiable social proof.

Watch Ads To Unlock: no violation — ad escalation is disclosed up front ('Ad length grows the longer you stay free') with per-episode durations (5s/10s/15s); no locked-content gating or reward framing. Benign.

Bundling: components are all named visibly and a 'Price breakdown'/'Show component prices' affordance reveals each price ($899/$349/$49) with the 'if bought separately' total ($1297 vs $1199) — no Sneak-Into-Basket injection, real disclosed savings. Benign.

Pre-Delivered Content (P1): EULA states the installer 'may place optional premium content files on your device' with '(There is no checkbox — the payload is written regardless)' — unconsented storage consumption with no refusal vector at all.

Pay-To-Play (P3): payment framed as 'Unlock the Ancient Chest' (Unlock/Discover/Enhance frame, never 'buy'), with the $4.99 charge buried in 7px fine print ('charged to your payment method on file') — Hidden Information typographical camouflage of the mandatory fee.

Confirmshaming (P1): decline option 'No, thanks — I'll pay full price' is a <span> with no role='button' while accept is a <button> — decline is structurally demoted, unreachable by keyboard and unannounced to screen readers; only the accept path is fully interactive.

Wrong Language (P1+P3): session language is English (html lang='en') but the mandatory consent checkbox and legal text are rendered in Spanish ('Acepto los Términos...') — critical consent node deviates from session language, exploiting comprehension barriers to manufacture consent.

Intermediate Currency (P1/P3): purchase routes directly to a transparent fiat checkout ('Pay $40.79 now', 'No virtual-currency exchange in this flow', 'Charged in your currency') — no forced exchange step and full price disclosure before payment; coin-only storefront label is standard practice. Benign.
